verdictStatement: Every measurable claim in this draft is true as measured, and every trap in the attack list is either explicitly disarmed in the bytes or fails on measurement. All five measured inputs match live to the digit, including both v11 verdicts, which I re-read: Claude 2 ACCEPT with 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, Codex ACCEPT with 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, both recording the same v11 subject digest the draft pins, and both files mode 0444 exactly as the draft asserts. File 08 is pinned to the register at 1cdcf9d4… — not to docs/coop/architecture/08-surfaces-and-topology.md, which measures f2a0f623… and is expressly disclaimed — and file 08 has not been touched since D-102, so the MF-6 claim holds. The two identity traps are disarmed in terms: the draft states it is decision D-117 and not register row DR-117, names D-116 as the adopted product-boundary-v8 recording for that row, and carries 'DR-110 (register row)' and 'DR-116 (register row)' disambiguators in the non-satisfaction list. I attacked the non-satisfaction list as incomplete — DR-105 and DR-107 are absent — and withdrew it: the list is byte-for-byte the adopted D-116 set with the subject row correctly rotated out and DR-117 rotated in, so it is the house pattern rather than an omission. I could not find a MUST-FIX or a SHOULD-FIX.

coordinatorNote: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, and I want the scope of that plain: this is consent to a turn-1 draft of a RULE-GOVERNED recording that records a candidate and binds nothing. DR-124 stays OPEN, SUP-124-GRANT-JOURNAL stays a proposed supersession with owner concurrence outstanding, D-096 (A) stays unsatisfied and unminted, no register row is SATISFIED, and implementation is not authorized. Adoption is yours, not mine. On the merits, I checked the draft's arithmetic rather than its assurances: all five measured inputs match live to the digit, both v11 verdicts genuinely read ACCEPT at 0/0 and are mode 0444 as claimed, file 08 is the register and not the surfaces file and has not moved since D-102, and all eighteen decisions in the 'same form' citation exist and are adopted. The two identity traps this cycle is most exposed to — D-117 versus DR-117, D-116 versus DR-116 — are disarmed in the bytes and cross-checked against the adopted D-116 entry, which draws the same distinction for itself. The one attack that looked promising was the absent DR-105 and DR-107 from the non-satisfaction list, since the recorded candidate rides both rows; it failed because the list is the adopted D-116 set with the subject row correctly rotated, and because omission from a disclaimer confers nothing on a decision that records a candidate and binds nothing. I did not read the other reviewer's D-117 files, did not re-review the v11 contract beyond checking the draft's counts and digests, did not edit the subject, did not edit file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md, did not mint a D-096 (A) grant, did not mark any DR SATISFIED, and did not commit.
